newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar, India discuss five mln tonne LNG supply.
newsitem.headline: Qatar, India discuss five mln tonne LNG supply.

text.p: Qatar is discussing selling around five million tonnes a year of liquified natural gas (LNG) to India, Qatari officials said on Wednesday.

"We have already signed a memorandum of understanding for 2.5 million tonnes with Essar Oil Ltd and are discussing for another 2 to 2.5 million tonnes of LNG supply with Gas Authority of India Ltd (GAIL)," said a top official at Qatar's Ministry of Energy and Industry.
"Two delegations from Essar and GAIL are coming to Doha on December 16 to pursue the negotiations and we hope to reach some sort of understanding then," he told Reuters.
GAIL has made an international call for supplies of LNG as part of a $10 billion project to diversify India's energy needs.

India's private Essar Oil signed the MOU with Ras Laffan LNG Company, one of Qatar's three multi-billion-dollar projects, in early 1995 to take 2.5 million tonnes of gas for 25 years from 2000. But the deal has not yet been converted into a firm sales and purchase agreement (SPA), crucial to win finance and make costly gas projects get-going.
Essar has until December 31 to transform the MOU into a SPA.

Qatar's Energy and Industry Minister Abdullah bin Hamad al-Attiyah told Reuters the Indian market was expanding "very fast" and "our estimate is that it will need up to five million tonnes of LNG by 2000 and much more after that."
The Qatari officials said the GAIL delegation would also discuss buying Qatari land crude on term contract basis, besides LNG supplies.
"Their need is urgent and they want to make provision for the period even before gas supplies could start," one said.
Qatar is presently implementing three major LNG projects to transform its mammoth gas reserves - the third largest in the world after Russia's and Iran's - into hard cash.

The first project - Qatar Liquefied Gas Company, or Qatargas has already gone on stream and is set to start shipping LNG to Japan from December 24. It is designed to produce six million tonnes a year, all dedicated to Japanese customers.
Ras Laffan LNG Company, or Rasgas, is expected to eventually produce 10 million tonnes a year and its first phase is due to start producing five million tonnes annually from July 1999.
Qatar-Enron LNG Marketing Company, designed to produce five million tonnes a year, is yet to start work on the ground.
